spans.s:
Pumāṃs denotes in the Rigveda^1 and later^2 man as the
‘male.’ It has no special reference to marriage like Pati, or to
heroism like Nṛ or Nara. In grammar it denotes the masculine
gender.^3
1) i. 124, 7; 162, 22; iii. 29, 13; iv. 3,
10, etc.
2) Av. iii. 6, 1; 23, 3; iv. 4, 4;
vi. 11, 2; Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, viii. 5,
etc.
3) Nirukta, iii. 8; Śatapatha Brāh-
maṇa, x. 1, 1, 8; 5, 1, 3; Cf. iv. 5, 2,
10, and puṃṣā nakṣatreṇa, ‘a Nakṣatra
with a masculine name,’ in the Bṛhad-
āraṇyaka Upaniṣad, vi. 3, 1.
